# Regional Hospital Stroke Capabilities (WWAMI)

Static, public-source reference map of hospital stroke-center certifications
(CSC / TSC / PSC / ASR), state stroke designations, and 24/7 endovascular
thrombectomy (EVT) capability across Washington, Alaska, Idaho, Montana, and
Wyoming, with transparent distance/transport planning estimates and a
user-adjustable expansion-planning heuristic. 236 hospitals.

- Site: https://rkalani1.github.io/telestroke-expansion-map/
- Source: https://github.com/rkalani1/telestroke-expansion-map

## Data

- /hospitals.json — the only dataset the app loads (schema 3.0.0). Top-level
  metadata: schema_version, data_version, last_verified, generated_at,
  primary_sources, coverage_note, census_snapshot, record_classes,
  certification_definitions, certifying_bodies.
- IMPORTANT — there are TWO record classes, and conflating them misreports the
  data. Each record carries recordClass and strokeDataStatus:
    * recordClass "stroke-capability" (135 records, strokeDataStatus
      "verified") — capability checked against primary sources. A null
      strokeCertificationType means CHECKED AND NONE FOUND.
    * recordClass "acute-care-census" (101 records, strokeDataStatus
      "not-assessed") — facility identity from the CMS acute-care census.
      strokeCertificationType is null and hasELVO is false because the site
      was NEVER ASSESSED. This is NOT evidence of absent capability. Do not
      count these as uncertified, and do not include them in certification
      rates or coverage-gap statistics.
- Per-record fields: id (primary key), cmsId (CMS CCN; may be null or shared),
  facilityIdType (ccn | shared-ccn | military), name, aliases, address, city,
  cityConfidence, county, state, zip, latitude, longitude, geocodePrecision,
  strokeCertificationType (CSC/TSC/PSC/ASR/null), certificationBasis
  (national | state | both | none | not-assessed), nationalCertification,
  stateDesignation, certifyingBody, certificationDetails, hasELVO,
  hospitalType, ownership, beds, healthSystem, dataSources, lastVerified.
- certificationBasis matters: 67 of the 135 assessed records display a tier
  derived from a WA ECS or Idaho TSE state designation alone, with no national
  accreditation. strokeCertificationType is this project's mapping onto the
  national ladder, not an accreditor's finding.
- Authoritative dates live inside hospitals.json. As of this file's last
  update: data_version 2026.08.15.1; stroke capability verified 2026-07-04
  (watch-list re-checked 2026-07-18); acute-care census snapshot Oct 2023.
  Certification and EVT changes require two independent public sources.
- /data/verification-worklist.csv — 56 ranked records that still need a
  primary-source check, with the source to check for each.
- /data/cms-census-wwami-2023-10.csv — the vendored CMS census subset.

## Methods

- /METHODOLOGY.md — scope and record classes (§1), certification nomenclature
  and the national-vs-state distinction (§3), transport-time model
  (haversine × 1.25 road factor; 55 mph ground + 8 min overhead; 150 mph air
  + 25 min overhead), expansion-scoring heuristic, integrity checks, limits.
- /CHANGELOG.md — release and data history.
- /COMPLIANCE.md — public-data boundary for this repository.

## Scope

Planning reference built from public sources (CMS, Joint Commission, DNV,
state registries). Not for clinical decision-making, live transfer routing,
or dispatch, and not an official state Department of Health product.
Absence of a certification on an acute-care-census record means the site was
not assessed, not that it lacks capability.
Transport times are order-of-magnitude planning estimates, not operational
dispatch times. Expansion scores are transparent heuristics computed in the
browser; they make no claims about clinical operations, staffing, volume, or
telestroke contract status.
